# Recorded Java Tic-Tac-Toe results

tictactoe-java.tsv contains 5,478 distinct positions exported on 2026-10-09
using public TAG commit d65ad79f04992e238663c37c812dc2c5f6ce7ff2. The user
reported a clean checkout. Java 21.0.12 and Maven 3.9.16 were used with an
authorised disposable copy; the reference checkout was not modified.

Generated by [ExportTicTacToe.java](../../tools/java-comparison/ExportTicTacToe.java)
and validated by tests/games/tictactoe/java_comparison.rs. Fixture schema v1 has four tab-separated
columns: recorded coordinate sequence, full-state signature, player-0 copy
signature and player-1 copy signature. Empty sequence means the initial board.
Move digits 0–8 encode x * 3 + y. Signature fields, separated by |, are board,
historical player, next player (-1 when finished), tick, completed turns, rounds,
first player, game status, both player results, both scores and ordered actions.
Actions are comma-separated move digits; board cells are x-major . / x / o.

Results cover one legal history per board, not all histories or invalid inputs.
The separate exhaustive Rust test checks every reachable transition. These are
recorded outputs, not runtime Java dependencies; cargo test --workspace includes
their comparison on any normal Rust checkout.

Regenerate into .scratch first using [comparison tooling](../../tools/java-comparison/README.md),
then compare with JAVA_TAG_FIXTURE before intentionally replacing this file.
Never regenerate expected results automatically from Rust rules. Investigate
differences and record any new reference version/cleanliness before accepting them.
Public source origins and MIT notice: [source notices](../../docs/source-notices.md).

The original Java export printed a javac archive-closing access diagnostic, but
the emitted exporter and runtime comparison succeeded. No access workaround used.
